title: Linkability of continuous sensor telemetry to user identity
description: Continuous GPS position, timestamps, and activity data captured by the wearable device can be linked to identify specific user movements, routines, and locations over time, potentially revealing patterns of life and behavior.

title: Identifiability through location and health data
description: The combination of GPS position data, timestamps, and biometric sensor readings (heart rate) can uniquely identify the user, especially when cross-referenced with other data sources or when the user's location is distinctive.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location information
description: Heart rate data, step counts, and GPS position are sensitive personal data that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, unauthorized access, or improper sharing with third parties.

title: Excessive data collection beyond necessity
description: Continuous collection of all sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS, timestamps) may exceed what is necessary for the device's intended function, violating data minimization principles.

title: Usurpation of user identity through biometric data
description: Heart rate and activity patterns captured continuously could potentially be used to impersonate the user or create unauthorized access credentials based on biometric behavior patterns.

title: Identification from GPS Traces
description: GPS traces transmitted from wearable device to companion app can be used to identify the user's precise location patterns, home/work addresses, and daily routines, enabling identification of the individual even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted with sufficient precision and is not anonymized

title: Linkability of Sensor Data
description: Sensor data batches (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) from the wearable device can be linked with other data sources (e.g., health records, social media, other apps) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Data is stored in a way that allows correlation across systems

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: Sensitive health and location data transmitted from wearable device to companion app may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels or stored without adequate encryption

title: Data Manipulation During Sync
description: Sensor data batches transmitted from wearable device to companion app could be altered, tampered with, or corrupted during the synchronization process, leading to inaccurate health records or misleading activity data.
assumptions: Data transmission or storage lacks integrity verification mechanisms

title: Unauthorized Access to App Data
description: Companion mobile app may be accessed by unauthorized users who can view or manipulate the synced sensor data, exercise sessions, and location information stored on the device.
assumptions: App lacks proper authentication, authorization, or encryption mechanisms

title: Linkability of health data across contexts
description: Calorie, meal, and weight data logged by the user could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially revealing patterns about their lifestyle, health status, or daily routines.

title: Identification of user from health data
description: Unique combinations of weight entries, meal patterns, and calorie intake could potentially be used to identify the specific user, especially if this data is shared or analyzed in conjunction with other datasets.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health data
description: The companion mobile app could disclose the user's calorie, meal, and weight data to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper sharing, or inadequate access controls.

title: Usurpation of user identity for data logging
description: An unauthorized person could potentially access the user's device or app account and log false calorie, meal, or weight entries on behalf of the user, compromising data integrity and privacy.

title: Linkability of Health Logs to Individuals
description: Health logs written by the companion mobile app could be linked to specific individuals through device identifiers, user accounts, or metadata, enabling tracking of individual health behaviors over time.
assumptions: The app maintains user accounts and device identifiers that can be correlated with health log entries.

title: Identifiability Through Health Log Content
description: Health logs containing calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions are inherently personal and could be used to identify specific users, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Health log data contains unique patterns or information that can distinguish individuals.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Logs
description: Health logs stored in the health log store could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: The data store may have insufficient access controls or encryption.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Health Logs
description: Health logs could be tampered with, modified, or deleted by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate health records and potential misuse of falsified data.
assumptions: The data store lacks adequate integrity controls or audit mechanisms.

title: Usurpation of User Identity for Health Log Access
description: Unauthorized users could potentially impersonate legitimate users to access or manipulate health logs through weak authentication mechanisms in the companion mobile app.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms in the app may be insufficient to prevent identity usurpation.

title: Non-compliance with Health Data Privacy Regulations
description: Storage and handling of health logs in the data store may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR or HIPAA due to inadequate consent management, data minimization, or retention policies.
assumptions: The system may not fully comply with applicable health data privacy regulations.

title: Linkability of Location Traces
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked to identify patterns in user movement, potentially revealing routines, habits, and associations between different locations and activities.
assumptions: Location data is stored in a format that preserves temporal and spatial relationships

title: Inference of Sensitive Information
description: Location history can be analyzed to infer sensitive information about the user, including home address, workplace, religious sites, medical facilities, political affiliations, and social relationships.
assumptions: Location data is sufficient to identify sensitive locations and patterns

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location history stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: DS2 has inadequate access controls or is vulnerable to external attacks

title: Tampering with Location Records
description: Location history data in DS2 could be altered, deleted, or falsified by attackers, compromising the integrity of the data and potentially enabling fraud or denial of service.
assumptions: DS2 lacks proper integrity controls and audit mechanisms

title: Usurpation of User Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the user and access or modify their location history, either by compromising the app or exploiting authentication weaknesses.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised

title: Identifiability of Health Log Data
description: The Health Analytics Service processes calorie, weight, and exercise logs that contain personally identifiable health information. Even with anonymization, the combination of multiple data points across sessions could potentially identify specific individuals.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to complete historical data across sessions

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: Health condition analysis data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data logging, or transmission vulnerabilities in the analytics service.
assumptions: Analytics service may have inadequate access controls or logging mechanisms

title: Linkability of Health Data Points
description: Multiple data points (calorie, weight, exercise logs across sessions) can be linked together to create detailed behavioral and health profiles of individuals, potentially revealing sensitive health conditions.
assumptions: Data is stored in a way that allows correlation across sessions

title: Unauthorized Use of Health Data
description: Health log data could be used for purposes beyond health-condition analysis, such as marketing, insurance underwriting, or third-party data sharing without user consent.
assumptions: Analytics service may share data with third parties or use data for secondary purposes

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing of health data may violate regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection laws if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Health data is subject to strict regulatory requirements

title: Location Data Linkability to Individual Identity
description: Location history data stored in DS2 can be linked to specific individuals across multiple sessions, enabling reconstruction of personal movement patterns and potentially revealing sensitive information about daily routines, social contacts, and locations visited.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for linkability threats in LINDDUN Pro, but exact node numbering may vary by version

title: Direct Identifiability from Location History
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) processes location history that can directly identify individuals through unique movement patterns, visit frequencies, and temporal data that distinguishes one person from another.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to distinguish between individuals
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for identifiability threats, but exact node numbering may vary by version

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Patterns
description: Derived daily routine and movement patterns from location history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches, revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to derived patterns that could be exfiltrated
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for disclosure threats, but exact node numbering may vary by version

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Collecting location history across multiple sessions may exceed what is necessary for deriving daily routine patterns, violating data minimization principles and collecting more personal data than required for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Daily routine can be derived from less granular or session-specific location data
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for data minimization threats, but exact node numbering may vary by version

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Location Data Handling
description: Processing of location history data may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) due to the sensitive nature of location data, lack of proper consent mechanisms, or insufficient data protection measures.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for non-compliance threats, but exact node numbering may vary by version

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health insights
description: Inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags transmitted from the Health Analytics Service to the Companion Mobile App could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels; app storage may lack adequate encryption.

title: Re-identification of health data recipients
description: The inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) could be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources or metadata.
assumptions: Health data is inherently sensitive and personally identifiable; users may not be fully anonymized.

title: Linkability of health insights to other data sources
description: Health insights received by the Companion Mobile App could be linked to other data sources (e.g., other apps, health records, device data) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated; user behavior patterns may be tracked across platforms.

title: Usurpation of user identity to access health insights
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a legitimate user to access the Companion Mobile App and retrieve sensitive health insights transmitted from the Health Analytics Service.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised; session hijacking or credential theft is possible.

title: Regulatory non-compliance for health data transmission
description: Transmission of inferred health insights may violate healthcare privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) if proper safeguards, consent mechanisms, or data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Health data is subject to strict regulatory requirements; current implementation may not meet compliance standards.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health indicators
description: The app displays eating-disorder and diabetes risk signals that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the app has access to sensitive health data and displays it to the user.

title: Direct identification of user's health conditions
description: The displayed health indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) directly identify the user's specific medical conditions, which is sensitive personal health information that could be misused.
assumptions: Assumes the health indicators are specific enough to identify the user's condition.

title: Linkability of health data with other data sources
description: The health indicators displayed could be linked with other data sources (e.g., medical records, insurance data, fitness tracking) to create a comprehensive health profile of the user.
assumptions: Assumes the health data could be correlated with other datasets.

title: Unauthorized access through user impersonation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the user to access their health data through the app, either by compromising credentials or exploiting authentication weaknesses.
assumptions: Assumes the app has authentication mechanisms that could be compromised.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider may disclose health and location data to unauthorized third parties, including government agencies, law enforcement, or commercial partners without proper consent or legal basis.

title: Individual Identifiability from Health Data
description: The full health and location dataset contains personally identifiable information that can be used to identify specific individuals, even with anonymization attempts.

title: Data Tampering by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider or their employees could modify, corrupt, or delete analytics data, models, or health records without detection.

title: Cross-Data Linkability
description: Health data, location data, and analytics models could be linked with other datasets held by the cloud provider to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Inappropriate Data Usage
description: The cloud provider may use the health and location data for purposes beyond the agreed analytics service, such as marketing, data selling, or research without explicit consent.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: The cloud provider may fail to comply with health data protection regulations (HIPAA, GDPR, etc.) regarding data hosting, access controls, and breach notification.
